legend: Giemsa staining of bone marrow aspirate smear in AML with inv(16), showing abnormal immature eosinophils with large basophilic granules seen admixed with myelomonocytic blasts.

Break-apart FISH showing an abnormal CBFB rearrangement signal pattern (one intact fusion signal, and one red signal separated from one green signal indicating a disruption), using a CBFB break-apart probe (<<30662>>). An interphase nucleus with an abnormal CBFB::MYH11 fusion signal pattern (one red signal for normal MYH11, one green signal for normal CBFB, and two CBFB::MYH11 fusion signals indicating an inversion or translocation), demonstrated using a CBFB::MYH11 dual-colour, dual-fusion probe. A normal nucleus is also present (two red signals for normal MYH11 and two green signals for normal CBFB) (<<30664>>).

Break-apart FISH showing an abnormal CBFB rearrangement signal pattern (one intact fusion signal, and one red signal separated from one green signal indicating a disruption), using a CBFB break-apart probe (<<30662>>). An interphase nucleus with an abnormal CBFB::MYH11 fusion signal pattern (one red signal for normal MYH11, one green signal for normal CBFB, and two CBFB::MYH11 fusion signals indicating an inversion or translocation), demonstrated using a CBFB::MYH11 dual-colour, dual-fusion probe. A normal nucleus is also present (two red signals for normal MYH11 and two green signals for normal CBFB) (<<30664>>).

Two blast cell populations are present: a more immature population with dim CD45 expression (blue), and a more mature and monocytic population with bright CD45 expression (red). Both populations express myeloid markers like CD13. The more immature population is expressing the progenitor cell marker CD34 and typically is asynchronously coexpressing the maturation-associated marker CD15. The more mature monocytic population is lacking CD34 expression and typically is aberrantly expressing the T-cell marker CD2. Normal lymphocytes and granulocytes are shown in grey.
Colon mucosal biopsy sample showing localization of inv(16) myeloid sarcoma.
